question: How can the exact-target Manager update reusable stock rows and dispatch generation-safe click events?
prototype_hypothesis: lvx_list_item_update(row, icon, primary, secondary, badge, compact); lv_obj_add_event_cb(object, callback, event_code, user_data); lv_event_get_user_data(event); lv_obj_set_hidden(object, hidden); lv_obj_align_to(object, base, align, x, y)
callsite_evidence: sub_C52C228 and sub_C52C2BC create stock rows, finalize layout, then register event code 7 through sub_C5882B8 with a bounded row index as user data
sub_C52C364 receives the event and recovers the same index through sub_C588600 before routing the action
sub_C53BF30 updates an existing list item through sub_C4A7BD0 and rebinds click handling without recreating the page root
sub_C4A7BD0 updates primary/secondary label children and trailing state stored in the stock row object
stock update paths call sub_C588458(object, 0/1) to show or hide existing child objects
sub_C54B0F4 creates multiple Settings rows under one page-content parent and calls sub_C588BE8(row, previous, 14, 0, 8) to place each row below its predecessor
control_flow_evidence: The target backend allocates rows only under the firmware-owned page root and retains pointers only in target-private storage
Each row callback carries only its bounded row index; generation, semantic key and event ID are read from the current binding table
canopus_ui_dispatch_event rejects stale generations and disabled actions before the Manager model executes an operation
Renders reuse rows by visual kind, hide unused rows, and explicitly align visible rows in a vertical chain, avoiding unproved concurrent object deletion
Informational text/status nodes use trailing_kind=0, interactive button/action nodes use the forward affordance trailing_kind=3, and switch rows use trailing_kind=1
sub_C4A74D4 maps trailing_kind=1 to the stock switch constructor sub_CA475B0; sub_C4A7BD0 applies checked/unchecked state through its final argument

The navigation page title and semantic text nodes are rendered as centered stock labels created through sub_C588338 and updated through sub_C588848, so a title like 'Canopus' is plain centered text rather than a button

Switch rows register the event on the trailing switch object returned by sub_C4A7F2C (row+0x50) for LV_EVENT_ALL (code 0) and dispatch only on LV_EVENT_VALUE_CHANGED (code 30), exactly matching the stock VAS alarm switch sub_C661410/sub_C6613C0; action/status rows register LV_EVENT_CLICKED (code 7) on the row like sub_C52C228
sub_C5886D0 lv_event_get_code filters delivered events so a switch toggle (VALUE_CHANGED) fires the semantic event directly while unrelated LVGL events are ignored
View changes that cross page boundaries are routed to the recovered page_goto/page_finish ABI (EVID-NAV-001) instead of rewriting rows in place
ownership_analysis: Rows remain children of the page root and are destroyed by the proven page lifecycle. Portable snapshots contain no firmware pointers. Target-private row pointers and bindings are cleared only after page destroy begins.
unsafe_assumptions: The update/show-hide/alignment path has strong stock callsite evidence but has not yet been exercised by the Canopus page on device
The firmware page root must expose the same scroll/content behavior as the recovered stock page-content parents when explicitly aligned children extend below the viewport

The stock label create/set-text thunks sub_C588338/sub_C588848 and the switch-row event registration on the trailing object are statically recovered; their exact default styling on the Manager page is device-gated
The backend is resident-first and does not unregister callbacks or unload code before reboot
recommended_probe: Open Overview, confirm the centered 'Canopus' title and description label, flip the Safe mode switch (it must toggle and then render disabled), tap Modules and a module row to verify real page transitions, pop with the system back gesture, enter and cancel a confirmation, verify no duplicate rows or stale callback dispatch, then close/reopen the app 100 times.
